concept: Select is the same recessed window as Input with a printed chevron, and it opens a plastic panel of options above the page; the chosen option is marked by a printed tick and weight, the way a selector on an appliance marks its setting in ink.

default_to_avoid.pattern: native browser select restyled, opening the operating system's menu
default_to_avoid.why_not: The open menu is drawn by the operating system, so its light, type and marking ignore the material and cannot follow dial's principles.

default_to_avoid.pattern: Radix or MUI select with a blue highlighted option
default_to_avoid.why_not: A tinted fill for the chosen option tells the state by colour alone and spends a hue that P1 keeps for one part per unit.

references.source: Braun T 1000 world receiver (Dieter Rams, 1963): a band selector whose chosen band is marked in printed ink on the case
Braun SK 4 radio-phonograph (Dieter Rams, Hans Gugelot, 1956): settings printed beside plain plastic parts, no coloured marking
WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices: select-only combobox pattern (https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/combobox/examples/combobox-select-only/)

derivation.consequence: the window is recessed into the body (inverse light)
derivation.form: The closed trigger is the same well as Input: surface.sunken with elevation.well and a line.ring hairline, full width of its column.

derivation.consequence: labels sit on the body's inset line, never floating mid-surface
derivation.form: The label is printed above the well at its start edge, and the placeholder is a separate grey prompt inside, never the name.

derivation.consequence: links, borders, icons, selections and charts never use it
derivation.form: The chosen option is marked by a printed tick glyph and medium weight in primary ink; no option row is ever filled orange or blue.
The open panel is surface.solid plastic with elevation.float and corner.inner, on layer.overlay above the page and nothing deeper.

derivation.consequence: every mechanism has its keyboard map
derivation.form: Arrows, Home, End, Page keys, type-ahead, Enter and Space select, and Escape closes and keeps focus on the trigger.

derivation.consequence: no entry choreography, no idle animation; transitions only on state
derivation.form: The panel rises out of the well when it opens and sinks back faster when it closes; a row inks in when it is reached, and nothing moves while the list sits open (D-008).

options.name: well with chevron, plastic panel opens below, tick + weight on the chosen option
band stepper: well between two round keys, no popup
panel opens over the well with the chosen option in place, index bar marks it

variants.reason: A keeps the label and the unit's display visible while the list is open and marks the choice with a printed tick and weight (P1 colour, P5 space); B makes a long list a chain of key presses with no type-ahead target, and C covers the label and the display above the field.

root.why: The field stacks its label above the well in one column, and anchors the panel to the well's edges.

label.why: The printed name uses the label size in medium weight, like the printing beside every other part of the unit.

trigger.why: The closed field is a recess with the inverse light, the same window that Input uses for typed text.

value.why: The chosen option is printed in primary ink on the sunken plastic at more than 4.5:1 in both themes.

placeholder.why: The prompt before a choice is secondary ink above 4.5:1, and it sits beside a printed label that stays.

chevron.why: The chevron is printed flat at the end of the well, a stroke of ink that tells the field opens a list.

panel.why: The open list is a plastic panel with one short soft shadow, above the page on the overlay layer and no further.

option.why: Every option row is at least 44px tall so a finger can pick it, with its text inset from the rounded ends.

tick.why: A printed tick in ink marks the chosen option, so the selection never uses the orange or any tinted fill.

text.why: Option words use the body size of the one grotesk, with a line box tall enough for stacked Thai marks.

md.why: The default well is 44px tall, the smallest target that every part in dial keeps for a finger.

lg.why: A 52px well with larger text for the main choice of a phone sheet held in one hand.

focus-visible.why: The trigger shows the same dark ring as every part, and keeps it while the list is open under it.

disabled.why: A disabled field loses its recess shadow and fades to half, so it reads as not taking a choice now.

aria-expanded=true.why: The chevron turns over on motion.release while the list is open, so the open state is seen arriving.

aria-selected=true.why: The chosen row is primary ink in medium weight with its tick, never a coloured fill behind the words.

data-active=true.why: The row under the keyboard or the pointer becomes a small recess, so the active row is shown by depth, not hue.

@media forced-colors: active.why: In forced colours the well and the panel keep real borders and the active row uses the system highlight.

data-state=open.why: Opening is a state change, so it moves. It rises in from @starting-style over motion.release on the decelerating curve (D-008).

data-state=closing.why: While it leaves, the part fades and sinks back over motion.exit on the accelerating curve, and no key or reader reaches it (D-008).

data-on=true.why: The part that now holds fades or folds in over motion.release, so the change is seen arriving (D-008).

@media prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.why: Under Reduce motion nothing travels; only fades remain, on motion.hover, which the tokens keep (D-008).

transform.why: Opening is a state change, so it moves. The panel fades up a rise (motion.rise) over motion.release on the decelerating curve, and leaves over motion.exit on the accelerating one, 0.5 × the way in (D-008). Under Reduce motion only the fade stays, on motion.hover.

opacity.why: Opening is a state change, so it moves. The panel fades up a rise (motion.rise) over motion.release on the decelerating curve, and leaves over motion.exit on the accelerating one, 0.5 × the way in (D-008). Under Reduce motion only the fade stays, on motion.hover.

background-color.why: The reached row sinks into a well and inks in on motion.hover, fast on and slower off, so the arrows read as walking down the list instead of jumping.

box-shadow.why: The reached row sinks into a well and inks in on motion.hover, fast on and slower off, so the arrows read as walking down the list instead of jumping.

color.why: The reached row sinks into a well and inks in on motion.hover, fast on and slower off, so the arrows read as walking down the list instead of jumping.
